The base template: menus, death and fallbacks

New games are seeded with editable boilerplate before the first room. Use it as a recommended starting point when it fits, or extend or replace any part to serve the brief. These are ordinary game resources, with no protected ownership or reserved template ranges.

- Logic 0 builds the menu bar once on boot (File: Save, Restore, Restart, Quit; Speed; Sound; Help), binds the classic keys (ESC opens the menu, F5/F7/F9 save, restore and restart, F1 shows help, TAB lists the inventory), turns the status line on, then runs call.v(v0) so your room logic runs first every cycle. After the room returns, logic 0 answers the menu controllers and, once per submitted line, prints the parser fallback: "I don't know the word" when the line carried an unknown word, "I don't understand that" when no said() matched. A room that answers a line without a said() match should set(f4) after its own reply so the template does not add the generic one.
- Death is a shared handler: print your death line, then call(255). It stops input and movement, plays the death sound and offers the Restore, Restart or Quit box — SPACE steps the choice, ENTER confirms, 1-3 choose directly, F7/F9/Alt-Z answer directly. A cancelled or failed restore returns to the box; the player stays dead rather than walking in a broken control mode. If you replace this handler, design and playtest the recovery or continuation behavior your game needs.
- Read logic 0 and logic 255 for their current state, controller and string usage before editing; their sources are available through read_logic. Update affected references together when reusing IDs or changing conventions. Automatic allocation avoids IDs used by the current code; explicit bindings and edits can coordinate a rewrite. Playtest boot, input and any menu/death behavior affected by your changes. A fair death still needs a fair cause: the hazard belongs in your room's picture and priority plane.

rooms.title: Castle Gate
rooms.description: Wenna starts outside Thornwall's gray castle. A royal notice (with a tarnished brass button hidden behind it), bread and a lit lantern are here. An alligator watches from the moat; swimming earns a warning, then death. Drawbridge north to the hall; the meadow road leads east.

rooms.title: Great Hall
rooms.description: King Brannoc sits by the kingdom's last candle. Talking to him after reading the notice accepts the errand (10). Returning with Bell, Ember and Map restores Thornwall and ends the game (60). South back to the gate.

rooms.title: Meadow Crossroads
rooms.description: A signpost where the meadow road splits. First roadside candle stands here, unlit (light it with the lantern). West to the castle, east to the river gorge, north to the old oak, south to the stove hut.

rooms.title: River Gorge
rooms.description: A heron stands on a rock and wants to discuss the bread. Giving it bread earns passage along the river (20); the heron then leads Wenna to where the Bell lies under the water and she recovers it (40). Second roadside candle. West to the crossroads.

rooms.title: Old Oak and Talking Well
rooms.description: An old woman knits map-thread under an oak; a talking well beside her gives hints. Answer her riddle to receive the wandering Map (40); wrong answers earn hints. She also gives a scrap of wool that can polish brass. Third roadside candle. South to the crossroads.

rooms.title: Stove Hut
rooms.description: A crooked hut with a smoking chimney and a vain salamander living in its stove. Showing it the polished brass button (its own reflection) persuades it to part with its undying Ember (40), carried in the lantern. North to the crossroads.

facts.name: premise
facts.text: Wenna, third squire of King Brannoc of Thornwall, must recover the Three Bright Things (Bell, Ember, Map) before the kingdom's last candle burns out. No hard timer: urgency is flavor.

facts.name: score
facts.text: Max score 230 (v7). 10 accept errand (hall), 20 help heron, 40 Bell, 40 Ember, 40 Map, 60 return all three, 20 relight all three roadside candles (rooms 3,4,5) before finishing.

facts.name: inventory
facts.text: Items: 0 royal notice (room 1), 1 loaf of bread (room 1), 2 lit lantern (room 1), 3 brass button (given on taking the notice), 4 Bell, 5 Ember, 6 Map. Brass button becomes polished via flag f_button_polished (wool from the old woman).

facts.name: ego
facts.text: View 1 is Wenna: short brown hair, rust-red tunic, oversized sleeves. Loops right, left, front, back.

facts.name: deaths
facts.text: Only death: swimming in the moat with the alligator in room 1, after a first warning. Wrong answers earn hints; treasures cannot be lost.

facts.name: clues
facts.text: The notice points to the hall. The alligator ignores bread; the heron wants it. The salamander loves polished brass. The talking well hints at the old woman's riddle. Lantern lights roadside candles.
